restrictions: Two-block ordinary collision attack of Guo, Liao, Liu, Liu, Qiao and Song (Journal of Cryptology 2020) on 5-round SHA3-256, with real collisions published: 2-round connector (428.8 core-hours, converted at the top of the quoted 2^20-2^22 full-round range: 2^44.821) plus 2^36.70 pairs (2^37.7 five-round evaluations); total 2^44.831, claimed 44.9.
Success probability 0.6 at time_log2 44.9 under H3; >= 0.39 at time_log2 45.544 without H3 (Markov).

heuristics.statement: The 3-round trail core No. 3 of the source holds with probability 2^-36.70 over the connector's affine message space, and the 2-round connector is solved within the reported 428.8 core-hours.
heuristics.scope: The cited attack of Journal of Cryptology 2020 (Guo, Liao, Liu, Liu, Qiao, Song), applied to this exact target (standard IV, full message, all digest bits).
heuristics.extrapolation: The source reports real 5-round SHA3-256 collisions (Table 17) found within the stated Tc and Tb.
heuristics.limitations: The trail probability and connector solving time are the source's empirical results; this package re-prices but does not re-derive them.

heuristics.statement: For a fresh free first block after the fixed prefix, the 2-round connector's linear system is solvable often enough that the source's reported connector time Tc (including its restarts) applies to this target.
heuristics.scope: The 5-round SHA3-256 connector of the source applied after the hashsmash prefix.
heuristics.extrapolation: The source found real 5-round SHA3-256 collisions with this two-block structure (Table 17).
heuristics.limitations: The first-block state has at most 1088 bits of input entropy, not a uniform 1600-bit state; only solvability of the connector is assumed.

heuristics.statement: Brute-force candidates from the connector's affine space and connector restarts behave as independent trials with a fixed per-trial success probability, so running for the expected work succeeds with probability at least 1-(1-1/n)^n.
heuristics.scope: The success probability 0.6 at time_log2 44.9 only.
heuristics.extrapolation: Without this premise Markov's inequality gives success >= 0.39 at time_log2 45.544.
heuristics.limitations: Not re-derived here; the assumption-free bound is stated alongside.
